## Motivation

GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash ship a `chat_template.jinja` that is costly to evaluate: tool results are matched to `tool_calls` by id with list rebuilding and sorting in Jinja, and every content part goes through macro calls. This PR renders both models' prompts with a Python port of the same template (adapted from the GLM team's reference implementation). It produces byte-identical prompts and renders 4.7-17x faster.

## Modifications

- **`parser/glm53_chat_template.py`**: one renderer for both models. GLM-5.3-Flash differs only in its multimodal block (image/video/audio parts emit `<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>`-style tokens where GLM-5.3 emits a text-only reminder) and in stringifying non-string tool-call names (`~` instead of `+`). Malformed input fails where the template fails (`ValueError` for Jinja's `UndefinedError`, the same `TypeError`), so the API still answers 400.
- **`parser/python_chat_template.py`**: `PythonChatTemplate` declares the features sglang otherwise derives from the Jinja source (content format, always-on reasoning, tool-result reordering, inline system messages, `glm45` / `glm47` parsers) and installs the renderer as the serving tokenizer's `apply_chat_template` with transformers' calling convention, so the request pipeline (content normalization, tool-result canonicalization, `continue_final_message`, the render cache) is unchanged.
- **Selection** (`TemplateManager`):
  - By default, the Python template replaces the checkpoint's when the architecture is `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` and the checkpoint template is a GLM-5.3 one whose multimodal block matches the architecture. GLM-5 / 5.1 / 5.2 share the architecture but not the template, so they keep Jinja.
  - `--chat-template glm-5.3` / `--chat-template glm-5.3-flash` forces it and needs no Jinja template.
  - `--chat-template <checkpoint>/chat_template.jinja` keeps the Jinja path exactly as before.
- **Auto parsers**: `--reasoning-parser auto` / `--tool-call-parser auto` resolve to the template's declared parsers when the Python template renders the prompts, as for the other non-Jinja encoders (DeepSeek-V4, Kimi-K3). A built-in template name resolves them without loading the tokenizer.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Differential fuzzing** against both checkpoints' `chat_template.jinja`, compiled the way transformers compiles it: ~490k randomized conversations (tools, parallel tool calls with out-of-order / duplicate / missing ids, `tool_reference`, reasoning history, `clear_thinking`, `reasoning_effort`, media parts, malformed messages). Every successful render is identical, and every failure fails on both sides with an error the API answers with 400 (never a 500).
- **Serving level**: `OpenAIServingChat._process_messages` with the real tokenizers gives identical prompts, prompt ids, media data and stops for 23 requests per model, on the default path, with `--chat-template glm-5.3[-flash]` and no Jinja template in the checkpoint, and with `--chat-template <jinja path>`.
- **Online A/B** (this branch vs. `main`, greedy decoding; GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 and GLM-5.3 TP8 on B200 with EAGLE MTP): identical `prompt_token_ids` and outputs for chat, `reasoning_effort`, multi-turn reasoning, `clear_thinking`, tools (`auto` / `required` / named / `none`), out-of-order tool results, inline system messages, `continue_final_message`, images, video, streaming, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages`, also with `--reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto`.
- **Unit tests**: `test/registered/unit/parser/test_glm53_chat_template.py`. Set `SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_CHECKPOINT` / `SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_FLASH_CHECKPOINT` to a model directory to also compare against its Jinja template.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Median latency with the GLM-5.3 tokenizer, prompts under 32,768 characters (below `SGLANG_PARALLEL_PROMPT_ENCODE_MIN_CHARS`, so the prompt is encoded with a single tokenizer call). Both implementations produce identical prompts and token ids in every row.

| Scenario | Prompt chars / tokens | Render, ms | Render + encode, ms | Request preprocessing, ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chat, 1 turn | 115 / 21 | 0.029 → 0.003 (9.1x) | 0.072 → 0.034 (2.1x) | 0.111 → 0.072 (1.5x) |
| chat, 20 turns with reasoning | 25,084 / 4,745 | 0.341 → 0.034 (10.1x) | 7.95 → 7.57 (1.05x) | 8.41 → 8.05 (1.04x) |
| 8 tools, 1 turn | 2,532 / 662 | 0.178 → 0.038 (4.7x) | 1.12 → 0.88 (1.3x) | 1.55 → 1.29 (1.2x) |
| agent: 8 tools, 18 tool-call rounds | 28,675 / 5,385 | 2.92 → 0.17 (17.1x) | 12.13 → 9.24 (1.3x) | 13.27 → 10.42 (1.3x) |
| agent: 8 tools, 8 rounds × 3 parallel calls | 31,556 / 5,921 | 2.60 → 0.16 (16.0x) | 12.54 → 9.94 (1.3x) | 13.71 → 11.14 (1.2x) |
| GLM-5.3-Flash, 8 images | 505 / 72 | 0.056 → 0.009 (6.3x) | 0.162 → 0.098 (1.7x) | 0.387 → 0.306 (1.3x) |

Longer prompts are encoded by `parallel_prompt_encode`, which takes the rendered string, so it applies to both implementations unchanged and saves the same encode time on both paths. Rendering then becomes the dominant remaining cost, and the Python template's gain in request preprocessing grows to 2.3x (GLM-5.3, identical token ids):

| Scenario | Prompt chars / tokens | Single-call encode (`SGLANG_PARALLEL_PROMPT_ENCODE=0`), ms | Parallel encode (default), ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| agent: 8 tools, 50 tool-call rounds | 73,404 / 13,449 | 32.20 → 25.16 (1.28x) | 12.72 → 5.45 (2.33x) |
| agent: 8 tools, 200 rounds × 3 parallel calls | 705,303 / 127,661 | 270.90 → 214.22 (1.26x) | 98.63 → 42.33 (2.33x) |

Together with parallel encode, request preprocessing for these prompts is 5.9x / 6.4x faster than Jinja with a single-call encode.

- Render is `tokenizer.apply_chat_template(..., tokenize=False)`, what sglang calls; render + encode adds `tokenizer.encode(add_special_tokens=False)`; request preprocessing is the whole `OpenAIServingChat._process_messages` (message normalization, render, encode), with the render cache cleared each iteration.
- GLM-5.3-Flash renders at the same speed; its request preprocessing also decodes the prompt for the multimodal processor, which adds up to ~1.9 ms on both sides.
- Rendering runs in Python under the GIL in the tokenizer manager (the Rust tokenizer releases it while encoding), so the saved render time also stops contending with other requests' processing.
- Environment: Intel Xeon 6960P, Python 3.12.15, transformers 5.19.0, jinja2 3.1.6, tokenizers 0.23.2.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,446 @@
+# Adapted from the GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash reference chat_template.py by Z.ai.
+"""Python version of the GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash chat templates.
+
+Both checkpoints ship a ``chat_template.jinja`` and the two templates are the
+same apart from one multimodal block, so a single renderer serves both:
+
+* GLM-5.3 is text-only. Image/video/audio content parts render a plain-prose
+  ``<reminder>`` sentence and never emit structural tokens, and the template's
+  ``'<tool_call>' + tc.name`` raises ``TypeError`` for a non-string name.
+* GLM-5.3-Flash adds the multimodal block: image and video parts render
+  ``<|begin_of_X|><|X|><|end_of_X|>`` (audio has no inner token), and its
+  ``'<tool_call>' ~ tc.name`` stringifies the name instead.
+
+The output is byte-identical to the Jinja templates. Where a template fails on
+malformed input, the renderer fails at the same point, raising ``ValueError``
+for Jinja's ``UndefinedError`` and the very ``TypeError`` Jinja would raise, so
+the serving layer answers both with 400 exactly as it did for the template.
+Jinja semantics that are easy to get wrong when reading the template source are
+called out inline; ``_UNDEFINED`` stands for Jinja's ``Undefined``.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any, Optional
+
+_UNDEFINED = object()
+
+_TOOLS_PREFIX = (
+    "<|system|>\n"
+    "# Tools\n\n"
+    "You may call one or more functions to assist with the user query.\n\n"
+    "You are provided with function signatures within <tools></tools> XML tags:\n"
+    "<tools>\n"
+)
+_TOOLS_SUFFIX = (
+    "</tools>\n\n"
+    "For each function call, output the function name and arguments within the "
+    "following XML format:\n"
+    "<tool_call>{function-name}<arg_key>{arg-key-1}</arg_key>"
+    "<arg_value>{arg-value-1}</arg_value><arg_key>{arg-key-2}</arg_key>"
+    "<arg_value>{arg-value-2}</arg_value>...</tool_call>"
+)
+
+# Tuples rather than sets: Jinja's `in` compares with ==, so an unhashable
+# part type must not raise here.
+_IMAGE_PART_TYPES = ("image", "image_url")
+_VIDEO_PART_TYPES = ("video", "video_url")
+_AUDIO_PART_TYPES = ("audio", "audio_url", "input_audio")
+_MEDIA_PART_TYPES = _IMAGE_PART_TYPES + _VIDEO_PART_TYPES + _AUDIO_PART_TYPES
+
+_MEDIA_REMINDER = (
+    "<reminder>You are unable to process this {} because you don't have "
+    "multi-modal input ability. Try different methods.</reminder>"
+)
+_IMAGE_TOKENS = "<|begin_of_image|><|image|><|end_of_image|>"
+_VIDEO_TOKENS = "<|begin_of_video|><|video|><|end_of_video|>"
+_AUDIO_TOKENS = "<|begin_of_audio|><|end_of_audio|>"
+
+
+def _get(obj: Any, key: str, default: Any = _UNDEFINED) -> Any:
+    """``obj.key`` in Jinja: an item of a mapping, an attribute otherwise."""
+    if isinstance(obj, Mapping):
+        return obj[key] if key in obj else default
+    return getattr(obj, key, default)
+
+
+def _first(value: Any) -> Any:
+    """``value.0`` in Jinja, which is Undefined when there is no item 0."""
+    try:
+        return value[0]
+    except (AttributeError, TypeError, LookupError):
+        return _UNDEFINED
+
+
+def _string(value: Any) -> str:
+    """``{{ value }}`` in Jinja: Undefined renders empty, None renders "None"."""
+    return "" if value is _UNDEFINED else str(value)
+
+
+def _is_iterable(value: Any) -> bool:
+    try:
+        iter(value)
+    except TypeError:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def _render_media(part_type: str, multimodal: bool) -> str:
+    if not multimodal:
+        media_type = part_type.replace("_url", "").replace("input_", "")
+        return _MEDIA_REMINDER.format(media_type)
+    if part_type in _IMAGE_PART_TYPES:
+        return _IMAGE_TOKENS
+    if part_type in _VIDEO_PART_TYPES:
+        return _VIDEO_TOKENS
+    return _AUDIO_TOKENS
+
+
+def _visible_text(content: Any, multimodal: bool) -> str:
+    if isinstance(content, str):
+        return content
+    if _is_iterable(content) and not isinstance(content, Mapping):
+        parts = []
+        for item in content:
+            if isinstance(item, Mapping):
+                part_type = _get(item, "type")
+                if part_type == "text":
+                    parts.append(_string(_get(item, "text")))
+                elif part_type in _MEDIA_PART_TYPES:
+                    parts.append(_render_media(part_type, multimodal))
+            elif isinstance(item, str):
+                parts.append(item)
+        return "".join(parts)
+    # The template guards this branch with `content is not none`, so None
+    # renders nothing instead of "None".
+    return "" if content is None else _string(content)
+
+
+def _unwrap_tool(tool: Any) -> Any:
+    # `'function' in tool` is a membership test, so a present but empty
+    # `function` still replaces the tool.
+    if isinstance(tool, Mapping) and "function" in tool:
+        return tool["function"]
+    return tool
+
+
+def _tool_to_json(tool: Any) -> str:
+    # The tool_to_json macro calls `tool.items()`, which fails on a non-mapping.
+    if not isinstance(tool, Mapping):
+        raise ValueError(f"Each tool must be a JSON object, got {type(tool).__name__}.")
+    # The macro writes `"{{ k }}": {{ v | tojson }}` by hand: values go through
+    # tojson (json.dumps under transformers), but keys are interpolated raw and
+    # are not JSON-escaped, so json.dumps on the whole dict would diverge.
+    fields = [
+        f'"{key!s}": {json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False)}'
+        for key, value in tool.items()
+        if key != "defer_loading" and key != "strict"
+    ]
+    return "{" + ", ".join(fields) + "}"
+
+
+def _tool_references_to_response(refs: Any, tools: Any) -> str:
+    # The template defines this macro under `{%- if tools -%}`, so rendering a
+    # tool_reference without tools called an undefined macro.
+    if not tools:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Rendering a tool_reference requires `tools`; the GLM-5.3 chat "
+            "template only defines its tool macros when tools are given."
+        )
+    parts = ["<tool_response><tools>\n"]
+    for ref in refs:
+        ref_name = _get(ref, "name")
+        for tool in tools:
+            tool = _unwrap_tool(tool)
+            # Undefined equals Undefined in Jinja, so a reference without a
+            # name matches every tool without one, as it does here.
+            if _get(tool, "name") == ref_name:
+                parts.append(_tool_to_json(tool) + "\n")
+    parts.append("</tools></tool_response>")
+    return "".join(parts)
+
+
+def _tool_response(text: str) -> str:
+    return "<tool_response>" + text + "</tool_response>"
+
+
+def _id_of(obj: Any) -> str:
+    tool_call_id = _get(obj, "tool_call_id", None)
+    if tool_call_id:
+        return str(tool_call_id)
+    obj_id = _get(obj, "id", None)
+    if obj_id:
+        return str(obj_id)
+    return ""
+
+
+def _is_list_of_outputs(message: Any) -> bool:
+    # `m.content and m.content.0.output is defined`: falsy content
+    # short-circuits, while reading `.output` from a missing item 0 (a mapping
+    # or a scalar content) raises UndefinedError.
+    content = _get(message, "content", None)
+    if not content:
+        return False
+    first = _first(content)
+    if first is _UNDEFINED:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "A tool message `content` must be a string or a list, got "
+            f"{type(content).__name__}."
+        )
+    return _get(first, "output") is not _UNDEFINED
+
+
+def _is_tool_reference_list(value: Any) -> bool:
+    # `v is iterable and v is not string and v is not mapping and v and
+    # v.0.type == "tool_reference"`; reading `.type` from a missing item 0
+    # raises UndefinedError like `_is_list_of_outputs`.
+    if isinstance(value, (str, Mapping)) or not _is_iterable(value) or not value:
+        return False
+    first = _first(value)
+    if first is _UNDEFINED:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"A tool_reference list must be a list, got {type(value).__name__}."
+        )
+    return _get(first, "type") == "tool_reference"
+
+
+def _render_output(entry: Any, tools: Any, multimodal: bool) -> str:
+    output = _get(entry, "output")
+    if _is_tool_reference_list(output):
+        return _tool_references_to_response(output, tools)
+    return _tool_response(_visible_text(output, multimodal))
+
+
+def _render_tool_response(message: Any, tools: Any, multimodal: bool) -> str:
+    content = _get(message, "content", None)
+    if isinstance(content, str):
+        return _tool_response(content)
+    if not isinstance(content, Mapping) and _is_tool_reference_list(content):
+        return _tool_references_to_response(content, tools)
+    if _is_list_of_outputs(message):
+        return "".join(_render_output(entry, tools, multimodal) for entry in content)
+    return _tool_response(_visible_text(content, multimodal))
+
+
+def _render_tool_block(
+    messages: list[Any], start: int, end: int, tools: Any, multimodal: bool
+) -> str:
+    """Render the consecutive tool messages ``messages[start:end + 1]``.
+
+    Results are reordered to follow the driving assistant's ``tool_calls`` when
+    every id is non-empty and unique on both sides and every result id names
+    one of the calls; otherwise they render in message order.

+"""Chat templates rendered in Python instead of the checkpoint's Jinja template.
+
+Some model families publish a reference ``chat_template.py`` alongside their
+``chat_template.jinja``. sglang carries such renderers and, when one applies to
+the served checkpoint, uses it in place of the Jinja template:
+
+* The serving tokenizer's ``apply_chat_template`` renders through Python, so
+  every caller keeps the transformers calling convention and the request
+  pipeline in front of it (content-part normalization, tool-result reordering,
+  ``continue_final_message``, the render cache) is unchanged.
+* The template features sglang would otherwise derive from the Jinja source
+  (content format, reasoning mode, tool-result reordering, inline system
+  messages and the parsers ``auto`` resolves to) are declared on the template
+  instead.
+"""
+

+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Optional

+from sglang.srt.parser.glm53_chat_template import render_glm53, render_glm53_flash

+    ReasoningToggleConfig,

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PythonChatTemplate:
+    """A chat template implemented in Python, with the features sglang needs.
+
+    ``render(messages, tools=None, add_generation_prompt=False, **kwargs)``
+    receives the same variables a Jinja template does and returns the prompt.
+    """

+    name: str
+    render: Callable[..., str]
+    content_format: str
+    reasoning_config: Optional[ReasoningToggleConfig]
+    may_reorder_tool_results: bool
+    supports_inline_system: bool
+    reasoning_parser: Optional[str] = None
+    tool_call_parser: Optional[str] = None
+
+    @property
+    def force_reasoning(self) -> bool:
+        return self.reasoning_config is not None and self.reasoning_config.always_on

+# from their Jinja source: list content parts, always-on reasoning (the
+# generation prompt opens <think> and there is no toggle), tool results matched

+_GLM53_FEATURES: Dict[str, Any] = dict(
+    content_format="openai",
+    reasoning_config=ReasoningToggleConfig(special_case="always"),
+    may_reorder_tool_results=True,

+    the model config for every other template.

+                chat_template=chat_template,
+                add_generation_prompt=add_generation_prompt,
+                continue_final_message=continue_final_message,
+                tokenize=tokenize,
+                padding=padding,
+                truncation=truncation,
+                max_length=max_length,
+                return_tensors=return_tensors,
+                return_dict=return_dict,
+                return_assistant_tokens_mask=return_assistant_tokens_mask,
+                tokenizer_kwargs=tokenizer_kwargs,
+                **kwargs,
+            )

+            raise ValueError(
+                "Cannot apply chat template to an empty conversation. Provide at "
+                "least one message."

+            rendered_chat,
+            padding=padding,
+            truncation=truncation,
+            max_length=max_length,
+            add_special_tokens=False,
+            return_tensors=return_tensors,
+            **(tokenizer_kwargs or {}),
+        )

+
+    tokenizer._sglang_jinja_apply_chat_template = jinja_apply_chat_template
+    tokenizer.apply_chat_template = apply_chat_template

+    """A reduced GLM-5.3 template with every construct template detection keys on."""
+    concat = "~" if multimodal else "+"

+        else ""
+    )
+    return (
+        "[gMASK]<sop>\n"
+        "{%- set effective_reasoning_effort = reasoning_effort if reasoning_effort is "
+        "defined and reasoning_effort in ['low', 'high'] else 'max' -%}"
+        "<|system|>Reasoning Effort: {{ effective_reasoning_effort | capitalize }}"
+        "{%- for m in messages -%}"
+        "{%- if m.role == 'system' -%}<|system|>{{ m.content }}"
+        "{%- elif m.role == 'user' -%}<|user|>"
+        "{%- if m.content is string -%}{{ m.content }}{%- else -%}"
+        "{%- for item in m.content -%}{%- if item.type == 'text' -%}{{ item.text }}"
+        f"{image}{{%- endif -%}}{{%- endfor -%}}{{%- endif -%}}"
+        "{%- elif m.role == 'tool' -%}<|observation|>{{ m.tool_call_id }}"
+        "{%- elif m.role == 'assistant' -%}<|assistant|>"
+        "{% for tc in m.tool_calls %}"
+        f"{{{{- '<tool_call>' {concat} tc.name -}}}}"
+        "{% for k, v in tc.arguments.items() %}<arg_key>{{ k }}</arg_key>"
+        "<arg_value>{{ v }}</arg_value>{% endfor %}</tool_call>{% endfor %}"
+        "{%- endif -%}{%- endfor -%}"
+        "{%- if add_generation_prompt -%}<|assistant|>{{- '<think>' -}}{%- endif -%}"
+    )

+    def test_other_templates_use_jinja_detection(self):
+        _, logs = self._resolve("GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM", GLM52_LIKE_TEMPLATE)
+        self.assertNotIn("Python chat template", logs)
+
+
+class TestInstallPythonChatTemplate(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        self.tokenizer = _tiny_tokenizer("{{ messages[0]['content'] }}!")
+        install_python_chat_template(self.tokenizer, GLM53)
+        self.messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Hi"}]
+        self.rendered = render_glm53(self.messages, add_generation_prompt=True)
+
+    def test_tokenizes_like_transformers(self):
+        ids = self.tokenizer(self.rendered, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
+        apply = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template
+        self.assertEqual(
+            apply(self.messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=False),
+            self.rendered,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            apply(self.messages, add_generation_prompt=True, return_dict=False), ids
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            apply(self.messages, add_generation_prompt=True)["input_ids"], ids
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            apply(
+                [self.messages, self.messages],
+                add_generation_prompt=True,
+                tokenize=False,
+            ),
+            [self.rendered, self.rendered],
+        )
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            apply([], tokenize=False)
+
+    def test_converts_callable_tools(self):
+        def get_weather(city: str):
+            """Get the weather.
+
+            Args:
+                city: The city.
+            """
+
+        prompt = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+            self.messages, tools=[get_weather], tokenize=False
+        )
+        self.assertIn('"name": "get_weather"', prompt)
+
+    def test_jinja_only_features_use_the_original_implementation(self):
+        apply = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template
+        self.assertEqual(
+            apply(
+                self.messages,
+                chat_template="{{ messages[0]['content'] }}?",
+                tokenize=False,
+            ),
+            "Hi?",
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(
+            apply(self.messages, continue_final_message=True, tokenize=False), "Hi"
+        )
+
+    def test_signature_matches_transformers(self):
+        original = inspect.signature(PreTrainedTokenizerFast.apply_chat_template)
+        installed = inspect.signature(self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template)
+        expected = [
+            (name, parameter.default)
+            for name, parameter in original.parameters.items()
+            if name != "self"
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            [
+                (name, parameter.default)
+                for name, parameter in installed.parameters.items()
+            ],
+            expected,
+        )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_CHECKPOINT")
+    or os.environ.get("SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_FLASH_CHECKPOINT"),
+    "set SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_CHECKPOINT / SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_FLASH_CHECKPOINT",
+)
+class TestAgainstCheckpointTemplates(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_checkpoint_jinja(self):
+        for env, render in (
+            ("SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_CHECKPOINT", render_glm53),
+            ("SGLANG_TEST_GLM53_FLASH_CHECKPOINT", render_glm53_flash),
+        ):
+            model_dir = os.environ.get(env)
+            if not model_dir:
+                continue
+            with open(
+                os.path.join(model_dir, "chat_template.jinja"), encoding="utf-8"
+            ) as f:
+                compiled = _compile_jinja_template(f.read())
+            for name, (kwargs, _, _) in CASES.items():
+                for add_generation_prompt in (False, True):
+                    with self.subTest(
+                        model=model_dir, case=name, gen=add_generation_prompt
+                    ):
+                        kwargs = {
+                            **kwargs,
+                            "add_generation_prompt": add_generation_prompt,
+                        }
+                        self.assertEqual(
+                            _render(render, kwargs), compiled.render(**kwargs)
+                        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
